cards.back: **Power** is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. Average power is work done divided by the time taken.
cards.hint: Think about how quickly, not how much.

cards.front: Which equation gives average power from work and time, and what do the symbols mean?
cards.back: $P=\frac{W}{\Delta t}$, where $P$ is power in **watts**, $W$ is work in joules, and $\Delta t$ is time in seconds.
cards.hint: Work divided by the time taken.

cards.front: How is power linked to force and speed when the force acts along the motion?
cards.back: $P=Fv$, power equals force times speed. If the force makes an angle $\theta$ with the velocity, use $P=Fv\cos\theta$.
cards.hint: Divide $Fd$ by time to see where it comes from.

cards.front: Why do two people doing the same work on stairs have different power outputs?
cards.back: The **time** taken is different. The runner does the same work in less time, so has greater power.
A **watt** is one joule of energy transferred per second, so $1\,\mathrm{W}=1\,\mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}$.

cards.front: What are the steps to find average power when a load is lifted at steady speed?
cards.back: 1) Find the work, $W=mg\Delta h$. 2) Divide by the time taken, $P=\frac{W}{\Delta t}$. 3) Substitute SI units and calculate.

cards.front: A 60 kg student climbs stairs that rise 3.0 m in 4.0 s at steady speed. What is the average power? Use $g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$.
A constant 2000 N force moves a car along its motion at a steady 25 m/s. What is the power?
cards.hint: The force is along the velocity, so use $P=Fv$.

cards.front: Does a car moving at steady speed have zero engine power?
cards.back: **No**. The engine force balances resistance, so the engine still does work against that resistance and delivers power.

cards.front: Does a higher power rating always mean a device uses more energy?
cards.back: **No**. Energy is $E=P\Delta t$, so a 20 W bulb on for 10 s uses 200 J, more than a 100 W bulb on for 1 s, which uses 100 J.
cards.hint: Energy depends on time as well as power.

cards.front: What does the slope of a graph of work against time show?
cards.back: The **power**, because slope equals work divided by time.
cards.hint: Slope is change in y over change in x.

cards.back: The **rate of energy transfer at a single moment**, found from $P=Fv\cos\theta$ using the velocity at that moment.
cards.hint: Think of one instant, not an average.

cards.front: A crane lifts a 500 kg load 12 m at steady speed in 20 s. What is the average power? Use $g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$.
cards.hint: Work first, then divide by time.
